newsitem.title: USA: Bermuda court rejects Kemper Re's EMLICO appeal.
newsitem.headline: Bermuda court rejects Kemper Re's EMLICO appeal.

text.p: A Bermuda court has dismissed Kemper Reinsurance Co's appeal of a decision regarding the 1995 relocation of Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co Ltd (EMLICO) to Bermuda from Massachusetts.
The Bermuda Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal on Tuesday, a spokesman for EMLICO's joint liquidators said on Wednesday.
EMLICO, whose sole policyholder was Connecticut-based General Electric Co, filed a petition for voluntary winding-up shortly after moving to Bermuda.
Kemper Re, a unit of Kemper Insurance Co, had argued that EMLICO moved to Bermuda fraudulently, to take advantage of the country's more favorable insolvency laws.
It was attempting to obtain a judicial review of Bermuda regulators' decision to authorize EMLICO's relocation.
Kemper and other reinsurers are embroiled in litigation over EMLICO's liquidation, which may affect how soon the claims of EMLICO's 400 reinsurers might be resolved.
A Massachusetts Supreme Court justice is expected to rule soon on whether the state's insurance commissioner will be appointed U.S. receiver of EMLICO.

The case -- which pits General Electric, EMLICO, regulators and liquidators against some of the world's biggest reinsurers -- is significant because it may have some bearing on to what degree insurers are allowed to restructure themselves in the face of massive environmental claims.

The Bermuda ruling "is another court decision in a long string of decisions that supports the redomestication of EMLICO, and the fact that this is essentially a commercial dispute," said Coleman Nee, a public relations consultant for General Electric.
He said Kemper Re and the other reinsurers were beginning to exhaust their legal options.
Spokespersons for Kemper Re were not immediately available for comment.
